To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) offline Monte-Carlo Tree-Search (MCTS) planning is a powerful tool for learning Atari games, and (b) offline MCTS planning is a useful source of data for training a deep learning-based real-time Atari game player.

(1) offline Monte-Carlo tree search planning can be used to train deep learning agents for real-time Atari game play; (2) the resulting agents achieve higher scores and win-streaks than DQN, and (3) they are able to learn from human play and achieve higher scores on games that are not available in the Arcade Learning Environment.

(1) the combination of offline planning and deep learning is effective at learning Atari game-playing agents; (2) the combination of Monte-Carlo Tree-Search and deep learning is particularly effective at learning Atari games; (3) offline Monte-Carlo Tree-search with deep learning outperforms all prior approaches on all Atari games.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) How can we combine model-free and planning based reinforcement learning to improve the performance of both approaches?
the question: Can we build a better Atari game playing agent?
the question of how best to combine model-free reinforcement learning and model-based reinforcement learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach, which is a combination of offline Monte-Carlo Tree-Search Planning and Deep Learning, is the best approach to play Atari Games in real time.
the combination of deep learning and planning-based methods is a promising direction for real-time game play.
the proposed method is able to outperform the DQN method in terms of the game score.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our agents are the first that combine the strengths of model-free deep learning and planning-based approaches, while avoiding their respective weaknesses.
we are using the slow planning-based agent to generate the training data and use it to train the fast model-free agent.
we propose a novel way of training a real-time agent using a planning-based approach, and that we show that this approach is better than the state-of-the-art.
The main takeaway from our work is that
model-free approaches, while very useful for learning, are not necessarily the best way to build real-time agents for games.
model-free reinforcement learning can be used to train planning-based agents to play games.
offline planning can provide useful data for deep learning agents.
